blocks.markdown: Insurance may be classified by the subject of the risk (life/non-life), the insured's relationship to the loss (first-party/third-party), who provides the protection (public/private), or the distribution model (such as microinsurance and bancassurance). These categories can overlap.
Life insurance: individual life

**Duplication note (D-02).** Sections 184–185 are quoted here as part of the individual-life series and again under ownership/transfer of life insurance in the second file. The fuller ownership/transfer treatment is in the policy lesson; both passages state the same statutory text (INS1 paras 70-73; INS2 paras 83-88).

blocks.markdown: Individual life — quick distinction: the insured person is covered under an individual policy. The amount payable is determined by the policy terms, and the Code includes special rules on suicide, policy transfer, minors' rights, and how the benefit is measured.
Group life

Group life insurance covers a group of people under one master policy, commonly arranged by an employer, association, lender, or other group policyholder. Individual members are usually given a certificate or statement describing their coverage. The existence of one master policy does not mean every member has identical rights in all circumstances; check eligibility, termination, conversion, beneficiary, and claims terms.

Simple example: an employer may buy a group life policy covering qualified employees. The employer is the master policyholder, while each covered employee is an insured member and may designate a beneficiary as provided in the policy and law.
Industrial life
Non-life: marine insurance
Non-life: fire insurance

**Trap.** Fire insurance can extend beyond fire itself, but the additional perils must be covered by the policy extension or a separate policy. Do not assume every fire policy automatically includes every natural disaster.
Non-life: casualty or liability insurance
Non-life: suretyship

There are three main roles: the principal/obligor must perform an obligation; the obligee is the person owed performance; and the surety guarantees performance if the principal defaults. The obligee may enforce the surety's liability as provided by the bond, but the amount is capped by the bond and the terms of the suretyship agreement.
Private vs. public insurance

Private insurance is commonly purchased from a private insurer licensed under the Insurance Code and is governed by the policy and applicable insurance law. Public or social insurance schemes are established or administered under special laws and public programs, such as SSS or GSIS benefits. These labels describe the provider and legal framework; a question may require identifying the particular enabling law rather than relying on labels alone.

**Exam cue.** Ask: Who administers the arrangement, what law created it, and what instrument defines the benefit? Do not assume every public benefit is an ordinary private insurance policy under RA No. 10607.
First-party vs. third-party insurance

First-party insurance covers the insured's own loss or property/health interest — for example, property insurance on one's home, own-damage motor coverage, or a health policy reimbursing the insured's medical expenses. Third-party insurance protects the insured against covered legal liability to another person — for example, motor-vehicle liability coverage responding to injury or property damage suffered by someone else. The injured third party is the person harmed; the policyholder is the insured whose liability is covered.
Microinsurance

Microinsurance is designed to make risk protection affordable for lower-income households. The statutory definition uses premium/contribution and benefit limits tied to the current Metro Manila minimum daily wage, so the actual peso amounts can change as wage rates change.
Bancassurance

Bancassurance is insurance sold to bank customers by an insurer within bank premises under Insurance Commission and BSP regulation. The bank does not have to own part of the insurer, but the required regulatory conditions must be satisfied, and the people presenting and selling insurance in the bank must have the appropriate license.
